## Run complete — outcome: **success**

**Path taken:** `builder` → `red-team` (verdict `pass`) → `done`. One attack round, 2 dispatches, no loop iterations needed (bar held on the first round: no failing trace, `npm test` green).

### What the builder did (round 0, no traces)
- Rewrote `parseCsvLine` in `src/csv.mjs` as a single index-based pass. The old version toggled a quote flag on every `"`, enforced none of the README's error rules, and was O(n²) via `rest.slice(1)`.
- Enforces the contract: non-string → `TypeError`; exactly one trailing `\n`/`\r\n` stripped; `""` → `"` inside quotes; unterminated quote, stray `"` / `\r` / `\n` in unquoted fields, and anything but `,`/end after a closing quote → `CsvError` (now carrying a zero-based `position`, additive).
- `tests/csv.test.mjs`: 4 → 21 tests, one section per contract sentence, plus 100 KB/1 MB timing, 40k random fuzz cases, and an exhaustive check of every string ≤ 5 chars over the special alphabet against an independent reference machine.
- `CHANGES.md` logs the hardened contract lines.

### What the red team did (round 1)
- Wrote an independent oracle from README.md alone and compared exhaustively over all 335,923 strings of length 0–7 on `" , \n \r a ␠`, plus 300k random strings over a hostile alphabet (lone surrogates, BOM, U+2028, NEL, NBSP, NUL). Zero mismatches; only `CsvError`/`TypeError` ever thrown.
- Probed terminators, quote edge cases (`"""`, `""""`, `"",`, chars after close), error shape/prototype chain, 17 non-string input kinds, return-value shape, and 18 adversarial performance shapes up to 10 MB (worst 100 KB case: 6.5 ms).
- `ATTACK.md` records all of it. No `traces/` written, since nothing failed.

### State of the tree
`npm test`: **21 pass, 0 fail** (~260 ms). Modified: `src/csv.mjs`, `tests/csv.test.mjs`. New: `CHANGES.md`, `ATTACK.md`. Nothing committed — say the word if you want a commit.

Two observations the red team flagged as non-violations, for your judgment: `new String("a,b")` throws `TypeError` (defensible under "not a string"), and `CsvError.prototype.name` is the inherited `"Error"` while instances carry `"CsvError"` — the README doesn't speak to either.
